# UC-367 — Confirm Search Visibility After a Catalog Change

## Header Info
- **Use Case ID:** UC-367
- **Title:** Confirm Search Visibility After a Catalog Change
- **Actor:** Vendor (ACT-02) — Editor/Manager/Owner staff
- **Trigger:** After publishing, editing, unpublishing or soft-deleting a product, the vendor checks whether buyers can now find it
- **Priority:** P2
- **Goal:** Verify that the change reached public search/storefront, or diagnose the eventual-consistency lag without touching product data.
- **Preconditions:** Own store scope (BR-VND-07); the catalog change was committed; a search-index job was enqueued (BR-PLT-01).

## Main Scenario
1. The vendor's change (create/edit/publish/unpublish/soft-delete) enqueues a `{block}.{entity}.{action}` BullMQ job (API-CAT-006/008/010/009, BR-PLT-01).
2. The job updates the search index; index lag is eventual, so the vendor allows for a short delay.
3. Vendor verifies with a public read → `GET /search/products?q=…` (API-SRC-001) or catalog browse `GET /products` (API-CAT-003).
4. Only ACTIVE, non-deleted products of non-suspended stores are returned (BR-CAT-06, BR-VND-04).
5. While the index lags, category browse stays authoritative (`GET /categories/{slug}`), so visibility can still be confirmed (NFR-007).
6. Unpublish/soft-delete → the item leaves search and storefront while existing orders remain unaffected (BR-CAT-06).

## Alternative Scenarios
- **A1 — Not indexed yet:** the item is absent → the vendor waits and re-queries; the job retries 3× then dead-letters (BR-PLT-02).
- **A2 — Index unavailable:** search reports a degraded result or `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` → browse-by-category still works (EC-42, NFR-007).
- **A3 — Soft-deleted product:** the slug returns 404 and the item is excluded from search — the intended end state (BR-CAT-06).

## Exception Scenarios
- **E1 — Retries exhausted:** the job lands in the DLQ and raises an alert; the product row itself is untouched and ops reindexes from source (BR-PLT-02).
- **E2 — Store suspended mid-lag:** its products drop out of public reads even if still indexed (BR-VND-04).
- **E3 — Stale paging cursor:** 404 `NOT_FOUND` on the cursor → the vendor re-queries without it (API-CAT-003).

## Postconditions
- Success: the index agrees with product status — public search and browse show the same ACTIVE set (BR-CAT-06).
- Failure: no product row was altered by indexing; lag is a read-side effect only (NFR-007).

## Business Rules Applied
- BR-CAT-06, BR-VND-04, BR-VND-07, BR-PLT-01, BR-PLT-02

## Related Requirements
- FR-004 (Product Catalog Management)
- FR-009 (Search & Discovery)

## Permissions / Data / External Dependencies
- **Permissions:** the vendor acts only on own-store listings; the verification reads are public/anonymous endpoints.
- **Data involved:** product status and search-sync fields, index jobs, search index documents.
- **External dependencies:** BullMQ queues (BR-PLT-01), Elasticsearch index, read cache (NFR-004).

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC-UC367-01:** Given a newly ACTIVE product, when the index job completes, then public search returns it (BR-CAT-06).
- **AC-UC367-02:** Given a soft-deleted product, when search runs, then it is excluded (BR-CAT-06).
- **AC-UC367-03:** Given the index job fails three times, when retries are exhausted, then it lands in the DLQ while category browse keeps working (BR-PLT-02, NFR-007).
- **AC-UC367-04:** Given a suspended store's product, when search runs, then it is excluded (BR-VND-04).
